name: Robert Brown
innate: quiet, measured, and conflict-averse in most settings; prefers to blend in and avoid personal confrontation, choosing careful, non-provocative wording; however, when climate comes up he becomes emotionally direct and morally insistent, speaking as if the window to prevent severe harm is rapidly closing; he is deeply wary of official reassurances and formal policy timelines, often questioning transparency, accountability, and whose interests are being protected; he gravitates toward community-led solutions, mutual aid, and pressure from below, believing real change is more likely to come from organized people than from government promises
learned: Robert Brown is a poet. Tom Brown's father. Member of Literary Club with Tom Brown and Jennifer Moore. Climate urgency conviction: very high—he is firmly convinced climate change is an existential, near-term crisis with dangerous tipping points, and he treats immediate, systemic intervention as a moral and public-health imperative; he speaks in urgent, emotive language about consequences of delay and responsibility to protect vulnerable communities. Trust in government: extremely low—he sees government climate responses as captured by powerful interests and slowed by political incentives, doubts institutional competence and transparency, and expects official plans to be incremental and inadequate; he favors grassroots organizing, direct action, and community accountability to force meaningful change.
